newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, bellies close with limit gains.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, bellies close with limit gains.

text.p: CME lean hog and pork belly futures closed with limit gains, and action in the respective options markets pointed to limit gains again at Tuesday's opening in deferred hog futures and most pork bellies, traders said.
Traders estimated about 2,600 limit bids in February hogs remained at the close, 1,500 in the April and 850 in the June. About 1,200 limit bids remained in February pork bellies and 300 in March.
USDA's bullish U.S. Hogs and Pigs report Friday was responsible for the gain.
USDA reported all hogs as of December 1 were 96 percent of a year ago and hogs kept for breeding at 97 percent. Both figures were less than analysts' expectations.

Analysts assembled by the CME after the report said the smaller hog supply could produce $60.00 cash hog prices in the first quarter of 1997 and $61.00 in the second quarter versus Monday's tops of $54.50 to $57.00 in Midwest markets.
Ron Plain, a University of Missouri agricultural economist, said producers in the Midwest did not have enough faith in the future of hog prices to enlarge herds.
"They possibly think there is a better future in selling corn then feeding it to hogs," he said.
Hogs closed up 2.00 cents in all but the distant June 1998 contract with February at a contract high of 79.500 cents per lb. Pork bellies were up 3.00 cents in all contracts with February at 80.425.
